title: qa-verify collateral.json, the proof that a fix breaks nothing else
description: Written by qa-verify fix-verify step 2b to <REPRO_DIR>/collateral.json (procedure: .claude/skills/qa-verify/references/collateral-proof.md, adapted from pstack's blast-radius, MIT). It backs MUST-HAVE 2 (no silent collateral change): fix-verify maps `status` to the no_collateral must-have (safe = pass, risky = fail, unproven and blocked = unknown). validate.py's QA-COLLATERAL-P1 ties the claimed rung to its evidence, so a 'ran it' claim without the command and output cannot validate.

status.description: safe = the safety fact reached rung 3 or deeper and no confirmed risk is rated high; risky = at least one confirmed risk; unproven = the safety fact stopped at rung 1 or 2; blocked = could not look (sandbox unreadable, diff missing).

change.description: What the change does, including the part the diff does not spell out.

statement.description: The one fact the change is safe because of.

ref.description: path:line (or library source) the fact rests on. Required from rung 2.

command.description: Rung 4: the exact command that ran the proof script.

output.description: Rung 4: what the script printed. Rung 5: the observed quote from the running app.

risks.description: Confirmed risks only. Cleared ones go in `cleared`.

check.description: How to check it, or the proof if it was run.

before_merge.description: The cheapest test or repro that catches the real bug, including the script written.
